newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euroboures nervous of Wall St, dollar firms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euroboures nervous of Wall St, dollar firms.

text.p: European bourses began mixed on Monday, nervous over developments across the Atlantic, where Wall Street suffered its third fall in a row on Friday after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's warning on lofty stock prices fuelled speculation about an interest rate hike.

On the currency front, the dollar was more than half a pfennig higher against the mark in early trading after a German Sunday newspaper report said a relentless rise in German unemployment continued in February.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, shares were moderately lower in early trade as market makers marked down prices after Wall Street's 47-point decline on Friday.
Dealers said weaker U.S. Treasuries and British bonds also unsettled early investor sentiment, as did growing political uncertainties ahead of the looming British general election.
"There isn't any panic this morning. Just a mark down," the head of trading at a major securities house said. "Considering Wall Street had a bad week, the FTSE hasn't done too badly."
The blue chip FTSE 100 index was down 14.4 points at 4,293.9 by 1000 GMT.
One big faller was NatWest Bank, as the stock went ex-dividend and in reaction to news last Friday that it had lost 50 million pounds ($81 million) on options trading.
Political worries ahead of a British election, due by May, were unsettling investor sentiment, dealers said.

"After last week's by-election (which the ruling Conservative Party lost by a big margin) people are starting to focus on the fact of a change of government," the head of trading at a major investment bank said.

"That, added to Wall Street's weakness, is keeping people away. Essentially there is no reason to buy this market at the moment. I think we could see the FTSE come off another 100 points before the buyers return," he said.
In Frankfurt, German shares opened bourse trade flat after moving mostly sideways in pre-bourse electronic dealings. Traders said there was a lack of significant market-moving information.

On the Paris bourse, French shares pushed higher at the opening, drawing comfort from a strong dollar versus the mark and shrugging off Wall Street's lower close, but later fell back to show limited gains.

The dollar firmed above 1.69 marks after Bild am Sonntag reported that German unemployment rose by 120,000 to a new postwar record of 4.8 million last month following a 500,000 rise in January. A rise of that magnitude would lift the jobless rate to 12.5 percent from 12.2 percent, the paper said.
Sharply divergent employment trends in Germany and the United States in recent months have been among the key driving forces behind the dollar/mark's surge higher this year.

"The leak of the German numbers should prove to be supportive for the dollar/mark and sterling/mark as well. But for the mark against the rest of Europe it is a bit of double-edged sword," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economic adviser at Bank of America.
News of a further spiral higher in German jobless numbers would support a recent widening in the U.S./German 10-year bond yield spread to more than 100 basis points.
However, it also makes it more difficult for Germany to meet 1997 budget deficit targets necessary to start European monetary union in 1999.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar was at 1.6920 marks and 120.65 yen, compared with 1.6885 and 120.88 in late European trade on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1000 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 14.4 points at 4,293.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 5.93 points at 2,612.74.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 0.74 points lower at 3,260.38.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened firmer at $362.50 from London's previous close of $358.45. Silver was higher at 532 cents.
($ = 0.615 British Pounds)
